hook_text: Every geometry problem is detective work. Four moves solve all of them, and the first move is the one everyone skips.
clip_script: A kite. Top corner 50, bottom corner 110, find the side corners. Here is the routine. Collect: the dashes say two pairs of neighbouring sides are equal, so it really is a kite. Name: kite. That one word unlocks a rule, the two side corners are equal. Chain: call them x. Four corners make 360, so 50 plus 110 plus x plus x is 360, 2x is 200, x is 100. Check: 50 plus 110 plus 100 plus 100 is 360. Done, with a reason on every line. Now a rhombus with a 70 corner. Collect: four equal sides. Name: rhombus, so neighbours add to 180 and the diagonals halve the corners and cross at 90. Chain: next corner 110, the diagonal makes 55 and 35, and the little triangle is 55, 35, 90. Check: 180. The move everyone skips is naming the shape, and the shape is where the rules live. Say it: collect, name, chain, check.
visual_style: A kite on a whiteboard with its dashes glowing one pair at a time; the word KITE stamps across the top; lines of working appear with reasons in brackets; then a rhombus repeats the routine faster with its diagonals lighting up.
pacing: Kite at speaking pace with each move announced, rhombus fast, the closing line slow.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for triangles inside quadrilaterals, sides from similar triangles and the error museum.
